name: Dr. Criativo Consent
author: drcriativo

sections.description:
Dr. Criativo Consent adds a cookie notice built for Brazil’s LGPD
(Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados):

  • Real blocking: Google Analytics, the Meta Pixel, ads and the like only run
    after the visitor accepts the matching category.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 already configured.
  • Proof of consent: every choice is stored with the date, the policy version
    and the categories accepted.
  • YouTube videos and Google Maps only load after consent, with a placeholder
    in their place.
  • Texts, colors and the cookie list are managed in the platform dashboard, with
    no need to touch the site’s code.

This plugin is the bridge between your WordPress and the Dr. Criativo Consent
platform. It requires an account, and the Free plan (free forever, 1 site)
works. Create one at https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/.

External services

This plugin depends on the Dr. Criativo Consent service, operated by Dr.
Criativo (David Weingärtner – Sistemas e Softwares, CNPJ 31.650.257/0001-12),
at https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/. Without it, the notice does not appear.

What is sent, and when:

  • On every page of the site, the visitor’s browser loads the notice script
    from https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/c/<identifier>.js. As with any file loaded
    from the internet, the server receives the visitor’s IP address and browser
    (user agent).
  • When the visitor makes a choice in the notice, the browser sends to
    https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/api/log.php the random consent identifier, the
    accepted or rejected categories, the policy version, the date, the page and the
    browser (user agent). The IP address is stored only as a hash with a
    site-specific salt, never in plain text.
  • On paid plans with the scanner enabled, the browser occasionally sends the
    names of the cookies and third-party services present on the page — never
    their values.
  • When an administrator opens the plugin settings screen, WordPress calls
    https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/api/verificar.php with the identifier and the
    site address, to show whether the installation is correct.

The plugin sends nothing about logged-in users, orders, forms or any other
WordPress data.

This plugin does not contact Google, Meta, Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, TikTok,
Pinterest, LinkedIn, Smartlook, RD Station, HubSpot, Trustindex, JivoChat or
Tawk.to. Those names appear only as labels: when a tracking tag is found on the
site, the plugin shows its name in the settings screen and in the cookie list,
so the site owner knows what is on the page and can decide what should wait for
consent. No request is ever made to those services by this plugin.

  • Terms of Use: https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/termos
  • Privacy Notice: https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/privacidade
  • Data Processing Addendum: https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/tratamento-de-dados
sections.installation:
1. Create an account at https://opt.drcriativo.com.br/ (the Free plan works).
  2. Install and activate the plugin.
  3. Under the Dr. Criativo Consent menu, paste the site identifier shown in
    the platform dashboard.
  4. Save. The screen itself checks whether the notice is loading before the
    tracking tags and shows the result.
sections.faq:
Do I need to pay?

No. The Free plan is free forever, for 1 site. Paid plans add the cookie scanner,
your brand colors, a data-subject rights page and more sites.

Does it work with a caching plugin?

Yes. The plugin tells LiteSpeed Cache not to defer or combine the notice script,
which must be the first one to run on the page.

What if the platform goes down?

The site keeps working normally. Without the script, the blocked tags simply do
not run — the site never tracks without consent.

Does it work with Elementor and other page builders?

Yes. The plugin catches the tracking tags pasted into a page builder’s custom
code field, which never go through a plugin and would otherwise escape the
block. Embedded YouTube videos and Google Maps are also replaced by a
“click to load” box until the visitor accepts.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. The cookies WooCommerce needs to keep the cart and the checkout working are
treated as necessary and never blocked. The notice does not touch the checkout
flow.

What does the plugin store about my visitors?

The choice itself: the categories accepted or rejected, the date, the policy
version and a random identifier. The IP address is stored only as a hash, never
in plain text. No name, e-mail, order or form data is ever sent.
sections.changelog:
1.9.3

  • Fixed a regression introduced in 1.9.2 that broke the WooCommerce checkout. The notice script was printed with wp_print_scripts() inside wp_head at -9999, which fired the global wp_print_scripts action before wp_enqueue_scripts. WooCommerce uses that action to localize woocommerce_params and wc_checkout_params; they were no longer printed (“woocommerce_params is not defined”) and the checkout coupon form stopped opening. The tag is now printed with wp_scripts()->do_items(), without firing the action.

1.9.2

  • The notice script is now loaded with wp_enqueue_script, printed early so it still runs before tracking tags; its attributes come from script_loader_tag.
  • The settings screen CSS and JavaScript use wp_add_inline_style() and wp_add_inline_script().
  • Every setting passed to register_setting() is sanitized.
  • The output buffers that rewrite the page are now explicitly closed at shutdown.
  • Readme: the external services section explains that the plugin never contacts Google, Meta or the other providers it labels.

1.9.1

  • First release in the official WordPress repository.
  • Blocks tracking tags before consent, including the ones that ignore Google Consent Mode (Meta Pixel, Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, TikTok, Pinterest, LinkedIn and Smartlook).
  • Google Consent Mode v2.
  • YouTube videos and Google Maps only load after consent.
  • Stores proof of every visitor’s choice.

screenshots.caption: The notice on a site: accepting and refusing have the same weight, and every word is written by the site owner in the dashboard.
The preference panel: each category can be turned off, and every one lists the cookies it uses.
The plugin screen: it checks by itself whether the notice loads before the tracking tags, and says so in plain language.
